answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with graduated trust tiers. Every new identity starts on the lowest terrace: strict rate limits and tiny transaction caps. Trust climbs only through sustained, peer-attested useful work, and it decays during inactivity, so a flood of fresh accounts stays powerless. High-value actions require a time-locked deposit in a shared vault, slashed on proven abuse. A Sybil farmer would need months of genuine work per identity, like growing a lotus from seed, making mass fakery cost more than it can ever earn.
